definition: Artists and repertoire: finding artists and choosing which records a label releases. At CircoLoco Records, Beatport says this sits with CircoLoco.
The studio Dan Houser and Lazlow Jones co-founded after leaving Rockstar.
Score tracks split into four to eight stems mixed live by gameplay, as in GTA Online: Los Santos Drug Wars, per the GTA wiki.
The July 2018 GTA Online update that let players buy and run nightclubs with four real resident DJs.
The roughly 26-minute GTA VI preview that premiered on Netflix on August 27, 2026.
A station picked and hosted by an outside artist, such as Flying Lotus's station in GTA V, built from unreleased music from his friends.
GTA V's rural conservative talk station, which only plays inside Blaine County.
Bertelsmann Music Group's video game arm in the 1990s. It published the first Grand Theft Auto in 1997 and was sold to Take-Two in 1998.
A New York Sunday party; its promoter John Davis partnered on Rockstar Loft, and Andi Hanley was a warm-up DJ there.
A multi-disc retail soundtrack with one disc per station: Vice City's seven CDs on Epic, San Andreas' eight discs on Interscope.
A flat one-time fee with no ongoing royalties.
A format where listeners phone the host; in GTA the callers are scripted, except some 2007 fan messages used on WKTT.
A real artist hosting as themselves (Iggy Pop) or voicing an invented DJ (Axl Rose as Tommy "The Nightmare" Smith).
GTA VI's on-demand shows for Jason and Lucia, playable in vehicles and on foot, announced as a series first in October 2026.
GTA III's only talk station, at 109 on the dial (outside the real FM band), where Lazlow plays himself taking calls from Liberty City's cranks.
The Monday party at DC10 in Ibiza, created in 1999 by Antonio Carbonaro and Andrea Pelino as a free Monday-morning after-party.
A record label announced on May 24, 2021 as a joint venture between CircoLoco and Rockstar Games.
The label's catalog prefix: CLR on records, retailers and Discogs; CRL in many RockstarINTEL headlines and on the GTA wiki. Same series.
Seth Troxler's mix unlocked by finding all four Monday Dreamin' EP media sticks.
The copyright in the song itself, its melody and words, usually owned by a music publisher. Also called publishing.
The club on Ibiza's Carretera de Salinas where CircoLoco runs, opened in the 1990s as a bar licensed for 80 people; capacity 1,500 today, per Wikipedia.
Reducing the heavy compression of modern masters so newer tracks sit beside older records on the same station.
Pulling a game from digital sale, often because its licenses have expired.
Ivan Pavlovich's title at Rockstar, which he joined in 2004; he leads music curation across games and GTA Online updates.
The Dundee studio that made the first Grand Theft Auto and later became Rockstar North.
Rockstar's term for music that changes with what happens in play, used in the GTA VI album announcement.
The 2009 standalone bundle of GTA IV's two episodes, The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony, with three exclusive stations.
The stretch when a track exists only in the game before it reaches streaming; about seven weeks for Dr. Dre's Contract songs.
A band or song written for the game and credited to an invented act, such as Love Fist on Vice City's V-Rock.
The band Bill Elm and Woody Jackson came from before scoring Red Dead Redemption.
A GTA 2 station tied to one gang's turf, such as Funami FM for the Yakuza or KGBH for the Russian mafia.
The German collective showcased on CLR 005, the 2023 various-artists record Anyway.
A 34-track original album made by Rockstar Games and Atlantic Records, announced September 17, 2026, for release with the game on November 19, 2026.
A small, fast patch. GTA V's 2026 Moloko removal arrived in one.
A short station-branding jingle or voice tag between songs, recorded after a station's tracks are chosen.
Unreleased music first heard on a GTA station, such as The Voidz on Kult FM or Dr. Dre's tracks in The Contract.
Songs written by the developer's own musicians and credited to fictional bands, as on GTA 1's seven stations.
The custom station in GTA IV on PC (and later Chinatown Wars on iOS and Android) that plays the player's own audio files.
Lazlow's pre-recorded, looping street-interview station in GTA IV and its episodes.
Vice City's celebrity interview and call-in station, hosted by Amy Sheckenhausen.
Moodymann's media-stick mix from Los Santos Tuners, found in his character Kenny's car at the LS Car Meet.
Rockstar's name for the GTA VI trailer released October 15, 2026; fans call it Trailer 3.
The in-game version of writer and host Lazlow Jones, written to be sadder and less like him with each game.
Liberty City Free Radio, the five-show talk station in Liberty City Stories, including a Chatterbox slot.
Unofficial early release of information, here through footage, a Spotify glitch or social posts; unconfirmed until Rockstar or the label says so.
GTA VI's fictional state, home to Vice City.
Music rights are bought for a fixed term; when they lapse, songs are patched out, as happened to GTA IV from April 26, 2018.
An existing commercial recording cleared for use in the game, the basis of Vice City's 1980s playlist.
The older looping next and previous station control, which could only step to the adjacent station.
A record with liquid sealed between clear layers; the GTA VI edition is two transparent magenta discs with blue liquid.
The After Hours station (LSUR) that loops the four residents' mixes and selections; it opened with a Solomun mix.
Donald Love's in-game company, owner of Chatterbox FM.
A film made inside a game engine, such as "The Introduction" on the San Andreas soundtrack DVD.
The copyright in one specific recording of a song, usually owned by a label.
Permission from a label to use a specific recording.
Processing every track so all stations sit at the same level and character, as on a real broadcast chain.
Which uses a license covers, such as in-game playback per platform, trailers or store pages.
A radio-wheel slot added with Los Santos Tuners in July 2021 that plays collectible media sticks.
An in-world collectible USB drive that unlocks a mix or EP in the Media Player.
Combining a cue's stems into a balanced mix; on GTA V Ivan Pavlovich did the mix-downs for each mission's eight stems, per Wikipedia.
The label's 20-track debut compilation, issued as Blue, Green, Violet and Black EPs in June 2021 and as an album on July 9, 2021.
Recording a performer's movement with suits and cameras to animate their character; Rockstar captured each resident playing a live set.
Take-Two's measure of sales booked in a period, including digital sales, and its main guidance figure.
The 2014 release of GTA V for newer consoles, which added about 165 radio tracks per the GTA wiki, 22 of them songs cut from the 2013 release.
CircoLoco's 20th-year slogan, which Antonio Carbonaro turned into a separate platform.
In-game shows for Jason and Lucia that can be played at any time, a first for the GTA series in VI.
A pre-agreed right to extend a license to sequels, DLC or ports.
Music composed for the game itself, separate from licensed radio; Justice are composing GTA VI's.
An in-world fictional product that mocks a real category, such as Sprunk soda or Pißwasser beer.
A license with no end date. It costs more and is described as rare in games.
A public-radio on-air fundraising appeal, parodied by VCPR's station managers.
Public Liberty Radio, GTA IV's public-radio parody, with The Seance, Pacemaker and Intelligent Agenda.
A streaming-service option that adds an unreleased album to your library automatically on release day.
Maurice Chavez's panel debate show on VCPR, with three-guest panels on topics such as public safety, morality and perception.
An artist voicing an in-game station's DJ character, such as Bad Bunny as El Martillo on Cocoteo FM.
The radial station picker introduced with GTA V and GTA Online: hold D-Pad Left (Q on PC) and hover to tune.
Crate-dug, lesser-known funk and soul; the format of San Andreas' Master Sounds 98.3.
DJ chatter that changes with time of day, weather or events in the game world, as Rockstar described for GTA IV in 2008.
The in-game studio at the center of The Contract's Dr. Dre storyline.
A real DJ recreated in GTA Online through motion capture, playing a custom mix in player-owned clubs.
Anyone who owns a share of a song or recording; one track can have six or more.
Stage name of rapper Jonathan Wilson, who refined and performed Craig Conner's in-house hip hop for GTA 1.
A New York club night Sam Houser and Terry Donovan started in 1999 with Body & Soul promoter John Davis; it wound down in 2000.
Rockstar's Scottish studio (Dundee, later Edinburgh), where GTA music and audio were overseen and mastered through the early games.
The entity named as owner of the CircoLoco Records trade name by the GTA wiki and RockstarINTEL; not checked against company filings.
GTA V's custom station for the player's own audio files, added with the PC version in April 2015.
An analytics firm whose models estimate digital sales; its GTA VI pre-order figures are estimates, not company data.
Units shipped to retailers plus digital sales, as Take-Two reports them; not the same as copies bought by players.
The person who sources and clears licensed tracks for a game; Pavlovich and Andi Hanley held the role on GTA IV.
A fake radio commercial for a parody brand, written in GTA III by Dan Houser and Lazlow and produced by Lazlow, per the GTA wiki.
The voice between tracks; in GTA IV and GTA V usually a real musician or DJ playing a version of themselves, such as Iggy Pop on Liberty Rock Radio or Flying Lotus on FlyLo FM.
The DJ links, station IDs and jokes between songs; the Vice City CDs kept them in.
One separate layer of a music cue, such as drums or bass, that the game brings in or drops out. GTA V missions used eight; Red Dead Redemption 2 went up to 15.
Joy Orbison's station from The Cayo Perico Heist, tied to a mission placing antennas around the map.
Permission from a music publisher to use a composition in a game or film.
A temporary playlist on an existing station, such as the Dre Day set on West Coast Classics, merged into its regular rotation in January 2022 per the GTA wiki.
All-speech GTA stations of scripted shows, callers and ads, which began in GTA III partly as a way to fill airtime cheaply.
A GTA radio station with no music, only scripted shows, call-ins and ads, such as Chatterbox FM, VCPR, WCTR or Integrity 2.0.
How long a license lasts. Reported game cases run from seven to 10 years.
The countries a license covers; worldwide costs more than a limited set.
An underground club beneath The Diamond Casino, added with The Cayo Perico Heist in December 2020, with Moodymann, Keinemusik and Palms Trax as residents.
Vice City Public Radio, a public-radio parody with guilt-trip pledge drives, home of Maurice Chavez's Pressing Issues in Vice City and Vice City Stories.
Red Dead Redemption 2 released its Daniel Lanois-produced songs and Woody Jackson's score as two separate albums in 2019.
West Coast Talk Radio, the Los Santos talk station in San Andreas (a full schedule of shows plus news) and GTA V (three shows).
GTA's parody news brand; in GTA IV its radio bulletins update as story missions are completed.
"We Know The Truth", GTA IV's right-wing talk station, home of The Richard Bastion Show.
